title: Interchanging proper direct image and extension by zero
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda$ be admissible in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], as fixed by the chapter. Let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper, let
$i:Y\to\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ be a compactification of
$i\circ p$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], with $\overline X$ dense in $W$. Then:

1. $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ (as open subschemes of $W$), and $r$ restricts to $p$
over $Y$;
2. for $A\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there is a unique map
$\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ in $D(\overline Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ whose
restriction to $Y$ is the identity of $Rp_*A$;
3. $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism for every $A\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Since $rj'=ip$, $j'$ factors through the open subscheme $V=r^{-1}(Y)$. The morphism $V\to Y$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence separated by the definition of proper in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The induced $Y$-morphism $\overline X\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], and has closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. It is an open immersion, since it is the restriction of the open immersion $j'$ to an open containing its image. Its image is dense in $V$: every nonempty open of $V$ is an open of $W$ and meets the dense image of $\overline X$. A closed dense subset is all of $V$. Thus this surjective open immersion identifies $\overline X$ with $r^{-1}(Y)$ as open subschemes, not merely as sets, and $r$ restricts to $p$.

All coefficient sheaves are pulled back from the same condensed $\Lambda$. The untwisted assertion of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies module pullback with sheaf inverse image with action transported along $\alpha_f^{-1}$, and makes it exact. This uses the chapter's finite-subextension condensed ring for $\Qlb$, not an identification with $C(-,\Qlb)$. By [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1),(4), the Cartesian square of step 1 has exact open functors and a natural isomorphism $r^*i_!\simeq j'_!p^*$ on module sheaves. Here all schemes are qcqs and both opens are quasi-compact. Apply these functors and this isomorphism termwise. [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supplies their functors on the unbounded derived categories, with their termwise models and shift isomorphisms. The same termwise open base-change isomorphism therefore identifies the derived functors $r^*i_!$ and $j'_!p^*$; its degreewise components commute with shifts.

source.place: Proof (2): restriction via exact open adjunction and its base-change isomorphism.

proof.text: The open adjunctions $i_!\dashv i^*$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ are adjunctions of additive functors, since all four are exact by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy](a) to obtain the adjunctions on complexes with degreewise units and counits. Their functors factor through the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms by step 2. Thus [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] gives $D(i_!)\dashv D(i^*)$ and $D(j'_!)\dashv D(j'^*)$ with the localized degreewise units and counits. Its normalization formulas also show that the open unit remains invertible, since the underived unit is invertible by [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1). The degreewise units and counits commute with the termwise shift isomorphisms. Finally [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] supplies $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ and $Lr^*\dashv Rr_*$; exactness from step 2 identifies these left derived pullbacks with $p^*$ and $r^*$.

source.place: Proof (2): the hidden termwise-adjunction and localization arguments, using Stacks 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives) and the Mathlib localization adjunction with its normalized unit and counit.

proof.text:
For $T\in D(Y,\Lambda)$ and $B\in D(W,\Lambda)$, compose the adjunction bijections of step 3 with the open base-change isomorphism of step 2:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^*Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_!T,Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(r^*i_!T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!p^*T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(p^*T,j'^*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*j'^*B).$$
This chain is natural in $T$ and $B$. Apply it and its inverse to the two identity arrows: naturality makes their composites identities. Hence it gives the natural restriction isomorphism $i^*Rr_*B\simeq Rp_*j'^*B$.

source.place: Proof (2): formal Hom calculation after the cited adjunction descent and open base change.

proof.text: For $B=j'_!A$ the unit isomorphism $j'^*j'_!A\simeq A$ of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf](1) and steps 2–4 give a natural identification $i^*Rr_*j'_!A\simeq Rp_*A$. Under the derived adjunction $i_!\dashv i^*$ constructed in steps 2–4, a map $i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ corresponds to its restriction composed with the unit $Rp_*A\to i^*i_!Rp_*A$, which is an isomorphism by the same node. Choose the map corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{Rp_*A}$. The bijection proves existence and uniqueness. This defines $\iota_A$ for every unbounded $A$. Write $F=i_!Rp_*$ and $G=Rr_*j'_!$. For $f:A\to A'$, both $G(f)\circ\iota_A$ and $\iota_{A'}\circ F(f)$ restrict to $Rp_*(f)$ under the natural identification of steps 2–4; the same adjunction bijection, now between $F(A)$ and $G(A')$, makes them equal. For an integer $n$, identify $F(A[n])$ with $F(A)[n]$ and $G(A[n])$ with $G(A)[n]$ using the derived shift isomorphisms. The shifted map $\iota_A[n]$ and $\iota_{A[n]}$ then both restrict to the identity of $Rp_*(A[n])$: the open base-change isomorphism and units in steps 2–4 are termwise maps, so commute with these shifts. Uniqueness gives their equality, proving compatibility with shifts as well as naturality.

source.place: Proof (2): identity under the open adjunction.

proof.text:
First take $A\in\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$. By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $j'_!A\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$. Let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be the closed complement of $Y$, let $W_Z=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, and write $c':W_Z\to W$ and $r_Z:W_Z\to Z$. These are again schemes and morphisms of the standing setting. Proper base change gives
$$c^*Rr_*j'_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*c'^*j'_!A.$$
For finite $\Lambda$ this is clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite]. For $\mathcal O_E$ it is clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral], and for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational]. The latter two apply since $\Dctf\subset\Dbc$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the cases $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ are $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By step 1, $W_Z$ misses $\overline X$. Clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] applied to $j'$ and $c'$ now identifies $c'^*j'_!$ with extension from the empty open, hence with zero (the sheaf axiom for the empty cover makes every module sheaf on the empty scheme zero). The same clause applied to $i$ and $c$ gives $c^*i_!=0$. Thus both restrictions of $\iota_A$ to $Z$ are maps between zero objects; its restriction to $Y$ is the identity by step 5.

source.place: Proof (3): proper base change and vanishing on the closed complement.

proof.text: The restrictions $i^*$ and $c^*$ are exact by the final untwisted assertion of the current [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], with coefficient actions transported along the inverse ring comparisons as in step 2. The cone of $\iota_A$ for $A\in\Dctf$ therefore has cohomology sheaves whose two restrictions vanish, by step 6. Each such sheaf is zero by [lem-exc-open-closed-detection], so the cone is acyclic and $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism. For the extension to $\Loc(\Dctf)$ use [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] first with compactification $(\mathrm{id}_{\overline X},p)$ to obtain exactness and coproduct preservation for $Rp_*$, then with $(i,\mathrm{id}_{\overline Y})$ for $i_!$, and with $(j',r)$ for $Rr_*j'_!$. Thus both functors $i_!Rp_*$ and $Rr_*j'_!$ have the hypotheses of [det-sf-determination-localizing]. The natural transformation $\iota$ commutes with shifts by step 5. Its invertibility locus contains $\Dctf$ by the preceding argument, so that cited determination lemma implies it contains all of $\Loc(\Dctf)$.

source.place: Proof (3): detection and propagation through localizing closure.

proof_origin.place: Proof clauses (1)–(3); clause (2) expanded through existing termwise-adjunction and localization theorems, followed by the formal Hom calculation.
